overview: Black sets up a c6 and d6 pawn pair against the c4-d4 centre, a Philidor- or Old-Indian-style set-up, and plans ...e5 or ...Nf6, ...Nbd7 and ...e5. White takes space with Nc3, e4 and Nf3 and plays against the passive Black bishop on c8. I am not sure of the main continuations, so this is reasoned from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: Take the full centre with Nc3, e4 and Nf3, keeping a space advantage.
Watch for ...e5 and meet it with dxe5 or d5, aiming at the c8-bishop.

black_ideas.idea: Develop ...Nf6, ...Nbd7 and ...e5 with a compact, Old Indian-like structure.
Possibly transpose to a Slav or Old Indian structure after ...Nf6 and ...Nbd7.

typical_structures.structure: Black's c6, d6 and e5 pawns against White's c4-d4-e4 centre, an Old Indian or Philidor type.

character.notes: Black's compact pawn set-up is hard to break down and play is quiet, though passive.

soundness.notes: Sound but slightly passive; White gets more space for free.

structure.notes: The centre is undecided until Black commits to ...e5 or ...Nf6; flexible.

approach.notes: A rare move order that strong players seldom pick; a surprise to dodge main lines.

level.notes: Plans are simple, but there is little theory and it demands handling a cramped game.

character.reason: Black has a compact pawn set-up and White has no early forcing play.

structure.reason: The centre is not yet decided after 2...d6.

approach.reason: A rare move order that strong players seldom choose.

level.reason: Simple plans but a cramped game to handle.

plans.reason: White's main benefit is space from the c4-d4-e4 centre.
